title: No terminal state for cross-project forwarded signals; no routing for moeb-source signals emitted during client project runs
description:
Two related gaps in signal lifecycle management:

1. When a moeb run on a client project (e.g. Ariadne) produces a signal with signal_source: 'moeb', that signal describes a deficiency in moeb itself — not in the client project. Currently there is no routing mechanism: the signal lands in the client's catalogue and stays there. moeb may already have a canonical consolidated signal for the same issue (e.g. a1000056 for read_file absolute path), but the client keeps a duplicate with no connection to it.

2. When a client project signal is manually or automatically forwarded to its owning project's catalogue, the client's local copy has no appropriate terminal status. The existing terminal states — resolved, archived, superseded — are all semantically wrong: the issue is not locally resolved, not stale/abandoned, and not replaced by a better local version. 'acknowledged' is the precise term: the issue is seen, recorded, and forwarded upstream; no local action is required or expected.

These two gaps mean every cross-project moeb run leaves orphaned signals in the client catalogue that are permanently inaccurate. Observed concretely: Ariadne accumulated 5 signals during moeb runs, all of which describe moeb deficiencies (absolute path read, bump_version hardcoding, phase ordering, Windows tag). All 5 required manual triage to identify as duplicates of existing or new moeb signals.
proposed_resolution:
1. Extend the signal status enum with a new terminal value 'acknowledged'. Acknowledged signals are excluded from the open signal count, never auto-selected by fix_signal, and rendered distinctly in the signal index (e.g. greyed out or in a separate 'forwarded' section). The acknowledgement relationship is recorded as a link entry (type 'forwarded_to') in the links array (established by a1000093), not as a top-level field. The link entry: { type: 'forwarded_to', signal_id: '<canonical signal ID in the owning project>', timestamp: '<ISO 8601 when forwarded>' }.

2. Add a routing rule to the signal emission flow: when a new signal is being written and signal_source does not match the current project's configured domain (e.g. signal_source 'moeb' emitted during an 'ariadne' run), the agent must: (a) check if an equivalent signal already exists in the owning project's catalogue (match by signal_id if known, or title similarity scan); (b) if a match exists, append the new occurrence to the existing owning-project signal rather than creating a new file; (c) if no match exists, write the signal directly to the owning project's catalogue path (if accessible) or queue it as an inter-project payload; (d) set the local copy to status 'acknowledged' with a forwarded_to link entry pointing to the canonical signal ID.

3. Update signal.schema.json to add 'acknowledged' to the status enum. The forwarded_to relationship is expressed via the links array (a1000093) — no new top-level fields are needed.

4. Update fix_signal.skill.md to skip acknowledged signals during signal selection.

5. Update the signal index generation to render acknowledged signals in a separate section.
